comments.content: Directed transactions are pushed by handle without a deep copy, unlike the random path (`t = new("rand")`) and the repro path (`iss.clone()` in the scoreboard). `vrf_axil_direct_lib::load()` returns references to the objects stored in its `static txn_t db[string][$]`, so the objects placed on the mailbox ARE the shared library prototypes. The driver writes back `obs_*`, `txn_result` and `check_enable` into them (e.g. `drive_write()` sets `check_enable=1'b0` on a reset interrupt), and `post_randomize()` is never called for directed txns, so no stale state is cleared. Consequently, re-loading/re-running the same directed case (multi-phase test, or calling `env.run()`/`body()` again) silently reuses a prototype whose `check_enable`/`txn_result`/`obs_*` were mutated by the previous run — the scoreboard can then skip the check (`n_skip++`) or compare against stale evidence, producing a wrong PASS/FAIL. Submitting the same prototype through both the sequence queue and `env.import_directed_queue()` would even put the identical handle on the bus twice. The txn class comment explicitly requires deep-copying before mailbox transfer; clone here.
